verdict.rationale: Letta ships an official Agent SDK (`@letta-ai/letta-agent-sdk`, confirmed in the GitHub repo) with first-party docs for agent creation, sessions and resume, typed streaming events, tool-permission callbacks, browser and React Native imports, cloud/local deployment backends, MCP tools, and demo apps. missing for 10: evidence of official SDKs beyond TypeScript (e.g. Python), independent or hands-on corroboration of SDK use.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can build against official SDKs

citations.quote: the Letta Agent SDK for building agents into TypeScript applications
Create a stateful agent with `client.createAgent()`. It returns the agent's ID as a string, which you use to open sessions and manage the agent later.
Send a message with `session.send()` and read the response with `session.stream()`. The stream yields typed events for the whole turn
Browser, Expo, and React Native applications must import the SDK from `@letta-ai/letta-agent-sdk/client`
Use `backend: "cloud"` to host agents in Letta Cloud and run tools in managed cloud environments.
